currentConcept.role: current concept: combine and divide two closed syllables into multisyllabic words
currentConcept.notes: Introductory and ongoing. The source begins with compound words and teaches four division rules: compound-word division, division between two consonants, one consonant assigned to close the first syllable, and three-consonant cases where a digraph stays together.

currentConcept.role: current concept: s may say /z/ between two vowels
currentConcept.notes: Source keyword/response is s-visit-/z/. It is added to the sound drill after being taught in Part 2.

currentConcept.role: subsequent concept: schwa/unexpected vowel sounds in unaccented closed syllables
currentConcept.notes: Subsequent Lessons concept. Source explains accented versus unaccented syllables and models schwa with words including level, wagon, common, seven, jacket, ticket, basket, and socket.

currentConcept.role: subsequent concept: five closed-syllable prefixes added to stand-alone base words
currentConcept.notes: After compound words, division rules, and schwa are mastered, introduce mid-, mis-, non-, trans-, and un-. The source also distinguishes tran- before a base element beginning with s.

currentConcept.role: current spelling procedure: segment, name, spell, and proofread multisyllabic words one syllable at a time
currentConcept.notes: This change in procedure is emphasized as central to Step 3. Sounds within a syllable are tapped only as needed.

sourceOrderedTeachingSequence.notes: Teach multisyllabic/closed-syllable reading and the four division rules first, including s=/z/ between vowels. Schwa and the five closed-syllable prefixes are explicitly Subsequent Lessons.

Introduce syllable-by-syllable spelling with compound words and taught division patterns, then double-consonant and final /ik/ spelling details, multisyllabic words with suffixes, and later prefix work as concepts are taught.

selectionRules: Drill all previously taught vowel Letter-Sound Cards and selected consonant/welded cards.
In the initial lesson(s), review learned sounds and move to Part 2.
After s-visit-/z/ is taught, include s-visit-/z/ in the drill.
Schwa is not added as a phoneme response; its notebook entry follows later schwa instruction.

contentRefs.role: Introductory/ongoing instruction for multisyllabic reading, four division rules, and s=/z/ between vowels
Subsequent instruction for schwa and five closed-syllable prefixes

selectionRules: Begin with 3-4 actual 2.5 review words.
Teach the four 3.1 division rules carefully; the source permits teaching them in separate lessons or combining them as appropriate.
Use compound words first to establish syllable-by-syllable decoding and left-to-right scooping.
Teach s-visit-/z/ as part of the early division sequence.
Do not introduce schwa/prefix work until the source's earlier division work is established.

contentRefs.role: current Word Card routine and category work

selectionRules: Begin with the existing previous-Substep fat stack.
Do not include 3.1 schwa or prefix Word Cards until those concepts have been taught.
Use current 3.1 Word Cards to practice left-to-right syllable decoding and category/syllable-division distinctions.
Review current 3.1 HFWs plus prior unmastered HFWs.

contentRefs.role: 3.1 compound, cactus/relish/mixed division, suffix, schwa, prefix, and nonsense-word lists
Part 4 practice/charting procedure and list types

selectionRules: Practice with 5-6 words from one current-substep list that reflects instruction already taught.
For charting, use another current-substep list reflecting instruction and select 15 words.
The source list types are compound words, cactus division, relish division, mixed division, +suffix, schwa, prefix + base word, and nonsense words.
Do not chart on a list type whose concept has not yet been explicitly taught.
Select an exact 3.1 sentence page that reflects concepts already taught and embed all 10 sentences.
Review HFWs/untaught words at the top of the page as needed.
Weave questions about division rules, syllable type, word elements, vocabulary, phrasing, and meaning.
Initially use previously taught vowel, consonant, and welded phonemes.
After s-visit-/z/ is taught, /z/ may prompt both z and s.
After prefixes are taught, include selected taught word elements as needed.

contentRefs.role: Introductory/ongoing spelling with the multisyllabic spelling procedure
spelling details for double consonants, final /ik/ = ic, suffixes, schwa, and taught prefixes

selectionRules: Begin with 3-4 actual 2.5 review words.
Dictate the whole multisyllabic word; student segments into syllables and names/spells one syllable at a time.
Use tapping within a syllable only when needed.
Teach double-consonant and final /ik/ = ic details in the source sequence.
For suffixed multisyllabic words, spell the word without the suffix first, one syllable at a time, then add the suffix.
Use closed-syllable prefixes only after they have been taught in Part 2.

contentRefs.role: Written Work Dictation and multisyllabic written procedure

selectionRules: Use source-verified Dictation Book items from concepts already taught in 3.1.
Use the multisyllabic spelling procedure for all multisyllabic written dictation.
After s=/z/ is taught, dictate /z/ with both z and s responses as appropriate.
Do not include schwa/prefix dictation before those concepts are taught.
Select the next unread 3.1 controlled passage in Reader sequence using the group's passage history.
If passage history is uncertain, flag it rather than infer it.
